c.tagline: Gateway to the reef, where Caribbean rhythm meets colonial charm.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are fixed by zone rather than metered; agree the price before riding, typically BZ$10-15 (about US$5-7.50) within the city.

emergency.note: 911 is the nationwide emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance in Belize.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: High crime; avoid the south side; most visitors transit quickly to the cays/interior

hood_desc: Belize City's most upscale district: a leafy waterfront quarter of colonial-era homes, embassies, the main museum, and the city's top resort-style hotels; best for first-time visitors wanting comfort and easy walking.
A breezy seafront boulevard lined with government buildings, the casino hotel, and quiet residential streets; suits travelers wanting sea views and a calmer pace close to Fort George.

The bustling colonial core around the Swing Bridge, markets, and Albert/Regent Streets; cheap and central but feels gritty and less safe after dark, so best for budget travelers comfortable with an urban vibe.
A quiet, mostly residential neighborhood a short taxi ride from downtown with a handful of boutique guesthouses; good for those wanting a calmer base near Princess Margaret Drive.
A leafy residential area along the road toward the airport, home to several B&Bs and inns; ideal for travelers wanting a peaceful stay convenient for early flights or airport transfers.

transit.pay: Intercity and local buses are paid in cash (BZD) to the driver or conductor on boarding. Water taxis to the cayes sell tickets at terminal counters in Fort George/Marine Parade, with online booking also available for the main operators.
transit.hours: Buses generally run roughly 5am-9pm with no true night service; water taxis operate multiple daily departures typically between about 6:30am and 5:30pm.
transit.note: Belize City has no metro, tram, or passenger rail; getting around is mostly on foot, by fixed-fare taxi, or via intercity buses and water taxis out to the cayes.

landmarks: Swing Bridge
One of the few manually operated swing bridges left in the world, this historic 1923 iron bridge over Haulover Creek is the symbolic heart of Belize City.
St. John's Cathedral
The oldest Anglican cathedral in Central America, this red-brick colonial church built by enslaved laborers is a striking historic landmark.
Belize City Lighthouse (Baron Bliss Memorial)
A picturesque white lighthouse on the waterfront honoring Baron Bliss, the city's great benefactor, offering classic harbor views.
Museum of Belize
Housed in a former colonial-era prison, this museum offers a photogenic blend of history and Maya artifacts in a distinctive brick building.
Government House / House of Culture
An elegant colonial mansion on the waterfront, once home to British governors, showcasing Belize City's colonial architectural heritage.
Fort George Lighthouse
A slender lighthouse marking the entrance to Belize City's harbor in the historic Fort George district, a favorite waterfront photo spot.
Marine Terminal (Belize City Waterfront)
The bustling harbor area where colorful water taxis depart for the cayes, offering vibrant scenes of Caribbean maritime life.
Battlefield Park
A lively central plaza surrounded by historic buildings and shops, the traditional gathering point and civic heart of downtown Belize City.
Image Factory Art Foundation
A creative hub in a historic wooden Caribbean building showcasing contemporary Belizean art, notable for its classic colonial architecture.
Yarborough Cemetery
British Honduras' first cemetery, used from 1787 to 1896, a narrow historic graveyard restored with a memorial wall naming early colonial-era residents.

train.note: Belize has no railway. Long-distance travel is by bus, water taxi or domestic flight.

bus.note: ADO runs a comfortable direct coach north to Chetumal and on to Cancún/Mérida; Fuente del Norte runs west to Flores (for Tikal) in Guatemala. Bring your passport and cash for border exit fees. Most buses use the Novelo's/main bus terminal on West Collet Canal Street.

intl.op: departs from San Pedro, not Belize City — San Pedro Belize Express

ferry.note: From Belize City the San Pedro Belize Express water taxi (Marine Terminal, North Front Street) is domestic — to Caye Caulker and San Pedro/Ambergris Caye; the international boat to Chetumal, Mexico leaves from San Pedro, so you connect there. Separately, small boats to Puerto Barrios/Livingston, Guatemala run from Punta Gorda in the far south, not from Belize City.
